body.statement: In the special case \(d=1\) and \(E=2\), \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=1\) implies \(A=\mathbb R\) and \(Q_A=0\), so the finite-breakout branch \(\mathcal B\) is empty.  For every \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\), the legal pair \(\theta,S\theta\) has the same observed laws \(\{P_e:e\in\mathcal E\}\) and the distinct effects \(\beta\) and \(\beta+\gamma/\alpha\), reproducing the simultaneous-noise nonidentification of Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, whenever this branch is nonempty.
body.justification: This reduction checks that the new frontier collapses to the closest known result at the two-environment boundary.
body.gap: This is already known from Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, and is included only as a fidelity reduction rather than a novelty claim.
body.consumer: It lets users interpret the new condition as a strict joint-environment rescue of the established two-environment obstruction.
body.proof_tex:
When \(d=1\) and \(E=2\), the matrix \(C\) has one row and one column.  The assumption \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=1\) says its column is nonzero, so
\[
 A=\operatorname{col}(C)=\mathbb R,
 \qquad
 Q_A=I_1-C(C^\top C)^{-1}C^\top=0.                  \tag{25}
\]
It follows from the definition of \(r^\star\) that \(r^\star=\infty\) for every calibrated parameter, and hence \(\mathcal B=\varnothing\).  Whenever a source-swap pair is legal, the identification-frontier theorem gives equality of its complete two-environment observed laws and distinct effects.  Thus the surviving branch has exactly the simultaneous-source label ambiguity stated in the proposition.  This is an algebraic derivation of the reduction; the comparison with Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, is not used as a proof premise.
